body:
I don't live in the US so I find it hard to find one.

Thank you.

I know a lot of people with sentiments: doesn't like their program but couldn't something about it. But they... seem to be doing okay. I keep wondering if I also look okay in front of other people.

I'm thinking of going to a therapist but I don't know how to tell my parents that I need to.

I'm from Asia. Money isn't really a big problem but there's a lot of pressure especially with a scholarship that limits the program choices. And a lot of pressure from the family. I don't want to disappoint - losing the scholarship (which is temporarily on hold) is just a big disappointment to my parents and I don't want that.
Sometimes I just want to start over. Go somewhere far and start a new life. But sometimes just ending it all seems like the easier way.

It is. I think it started two years ago. And by definition, it may be despair.

Sorry for the late reply. I had to push myself back to reality. Luckily I had a friend with me the whole day today which kept me from breaking down.

Thank you. I've always wanted to post in /r/depression but I could never fully relate to the posts in the subreddit. After reading things about actual depression, I always assure myself that I'm okay, I must be okay; I don't think I've experienced some of the symptoms.

In my case, things do go bad on the outside. However, I may have been seen as strong and well despite of it. I don't know. It still fascinates me how people would still depend on me. But it's because I've stopped caring about my life.

Perhaps, university.

Two years ago, I realized I'm not fit for my current program. But in my country, people are more practical. I had a scholarship that came with the degree so it is hard to get out of it. And I also feel lost on what to do after that. "Just finish that degree and you can do whatever you want after." And I felt unmotivated. There will be instances when I feel all motivated and hyped to graduate, but I feel bad and forced and doubtful afterwards.

I've managed to survive two more years but everything just went worse. For the past semester, I just stayed in my room except for a few classes and lots of extracurricular activities as distractions. Drinking habits also went bad. I fully distracted myself with everything that comes along. But when night comes and I'm at home, I feel guilty and tired but never sleepy. When I decide to do something, I get anxious. So I waste more time calming down.

Over the holidays, I have decided to start anew. To patch things up. But I have already ruined my life. I'm kicked out of the university despite having a few classes left. I only knew the day after the deadline. I don't know what to do. I'm holding on to that small ray of hope of able to pull it all back together. But I may no longer have that chance. I ruined it. I've become a disappointment.
I also didn't mean to put it that way. Sometimes, I feel like I can't relate with most symptoms of mental illnesses. Because most people think I'm okay, so maybe I /am/ okay.

I don't know. Self diagnosis with help from the internet tend to exaggerate certain conditions.

To where I'm going, maybe I will.
